title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck has built the analytic universal family over the upper half plane D^+. It is X_{D^+} = (D^+ x C)/Z^2, with (m,n) acting by (tau,z) -> (tau, z+m+n tau). He has shown it is a universal covering of the modular stack M_{1,1} for the 'strict Torelli rigidification', with deck group SL(2,Z) acting by Moebius transformations.

Top of page. He reconciles the Moebius action with the modular description. Here 'tau' also denotes a Torelli marking, an oriented isomorphism Z^2 -> H_1(E,Z). The formula is g.tau = tau o tau_inf(g^{-1}), with tau_inf = diag(-1,1) in GL(2,Z). The map g -> tau_inf(g^{-1}) is inversion followed by conjugation by diag(-1,1); it sends (a b; c d) to (d b; c a). Being an anti-automorphism, it turns the natural right action of SL(2,Z) on markings (precomposition) into a left action. Check: g^{-1} = (d -b; -c a), and conjugating by diag(-1,1) flips the off-diagonal signs, giving (d b; c a). The next page confirms the conventions: (z1,z2) -> (d z1 + c z2, b z1 + a z2), so z2/z1 -> (a tau + b)/(c tau + d). The page is internally consistent.

Corollary 1. The fundamental group T_{1,1} of the stack M_{1,1}, relative to this universal cover, is canonically SL(2,Z) (not PSL, since -1 is the generic automorphism of an elliptic curve). The left action comes from the canonical right action by g -> g^{-1}.

Corollary 2. This is the topological counterpart, via the identification of the Teichmueller groups T_{g,nu} with pi_1 of M_{g,nu}. For a compact oriented genus-1 surface (X,o), where o is the orientation, the mapping class group T maps isomorphically to Aut^+_Z(H) = SL(2,Z), with H = pi_1 = H_1(X,Z).

Corollary 3. This is the purely algebraic counterpart. For pi a discrete 'groupe a lacets' of type (1,1), i.e. a free group on 2 generators with the distinguished conjugacy class of the puncture loop, the group of orientation-compatible outer automorphisms preserving the loop structure maps isomorphically onto Aut^+(pi_ab) = SL(2,Z). This is the Dehn-Nielsen statement for the once-punctured torus.

Purpose: to set up the transcendental, complex-analytic description of M_{1,1} and its Teichmueller group. This serves as the base case of the Teichmueller-tower program, and is then extended to the birigidified (Torelli + differential) family on PD^+.
errors: Notational overload: 'tau' denotes both the point of D^+ and the Torelli marking (and tau_inf a matrix), but the formula is correct once read as an action on markings.

In Corollary 2, 'o' is the orientation, not a base point; this is harmless since pi_1 of the torus is abelian. The deduction of Cor. 2 and Cor. 3 from Cor. 1 relies on the identification of T_{g,nu} with the analytic pi_1 of M_{g,nu}, which is assumed rather than proved here.
Previous page writes D^* for D^+ (slip).

ideas.what: Converting the right action of SL(2,Z) on Torelli markings into the left Moebius action via the anti-automorphism g -> diag(-1,1) g^{-1} diag(-1,1)
ideas.modern_name: action of SL(2,Z) on framed lattices / period matrices

ideas.what: pi_1 of the modular stack M_{1,1} is SL(2,Z), with the upper half plane as universal cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; stack viewpoint Deligne-Mumford 1969 and later

ideas.what: Mapping class group of the torus equals SL(2,Z)
Outer automorphisms of a type-(1,1) group with loops, compatible with orientation, correspond to SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: Dehn-Nielsen-Baer for the once-punctured torus; Out^+(F_2) = SL(2,Z) (Nielsen)
ideas.where_published: 'groupes a lacets' are alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme, but this corollary is not stated there to my knowledge

deep.surprise_reason: These are classical facts (Dehn-Nielsen, uniformization of M_{1,1}) recast in Grothendieck's modular/Teichmueller-tower language. The only mildly distinctive feature is deducing topological and group-theoretic statements from the analytic modular stack, a known Grothendieckian stance. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Soient pi un groupe : lacets de type (1,1)' should read 'Soient pi un groupe a lacets de type (1,1)': the ':' is the handwritten 'a'.
'le groupe des autom. ext : lacets de pi' should read 'le groupe des autom. ext. a lacets de pi', i.e. outer automorphisms respecting the loop structure.
'deduit de l'operation canonique a droite' is correct, with 'a' added above the line.
Top line: 'ou' before tau_inf is 'ou' (where); the second relation ends with 'si g = (a b; c d)'.
